name: EVA
summary: A balloon-neutrino mission concept developed a large radio reflector integrated into the balloon surface. Feasibility studies and a scale-model hang test were performed, while a full EVA neutrino science flight is not established.
detection_principle: An equatorial reflecting band on a super-pressure balloon would focus impulsive radio signals onto an internal antenna feed array. It would observe Askaryan pulses from neutrino showers in Antarctic ice and geomagnetic emission from cosmic-ray air showers.

status.label: Status not established
status.evidence: The available programme evidence documents a historical mission concept and scale-model R&D. A full EVA science flight or a precise current project disposition is not established.

timeline.event: Mission design and simulated performance published; NASA development grant announced.
Feasibility and scale-model test results reported.

key_parameters.value: Balloon-surface toroidal reflector with an internal membrane-mounted feed array

key_parameters.name: Implemented development test
key_parameters.value: 1:20-scale hang test, reported in the 2016 update

results.summary: A 1:20-scale model demonstrated focusing in a ground hang test. Predicted event yields in a future balloon flight are simulations, not measured neutrino events.

science_scope: Published limits are not neutrino detections. Instrument or exposure parameters refer to the explicitly named campaign; research prototypes and future designs are distinguished.
